American Discovery 250 Relay to pass through Park Forest and Matteson on Oct. 13
The American Discovery 250 Relay honoring America’s semiquincentennial will stop in Park Forest and Matteson on Oct. 13 with a public celebration at Holden Park. Residents can join by participating along local trails or attending festivities featuring food and games.
The American Discovery 250 Relay, a cross-country event commemorating the nation’s 250th anniversary, will pass through Park Forest and Matteson on Tuesday, Oct. 13, giving local residents an opportunity to participate in a historic celebration.
Park Forest and Matteson will jointly welcome the relay as participants carry a copy of the Declaration of Independence along the American Discovery Trail. A community celebration is scheduled from noon to 2 p.m. at Holden Park in Matteson near the Old Plank Road Trail, with all residents invited to attend.
The event will include food, games, and giveaways for attendees. Matteson plans to serve apple pie, drinks, and chips while Park Forest will provide hot dogs and additional giveaways. Area schools have also been invited to join in the festivities. Organizers said that the relay is not a race but rather "a celebration of American history, culture, nature, and the communities along the trail." Participants are traveling by walking, running, biking or other nonmotorized means.
The American Discovery 250 Relay began July 4 at California’s Golden Gate Bridge and will conclude on Thanksgiving Day at Delaware’s Atlantic coast after traversing approximately 6,800 miles across fifteen states via routes including Illinois’ northern corridor. The trail connects communities and historic sites managed by various local, state and federal agencies; more than forty million people live near its path, according to organizers.
Residents are encouraged to walk or bike alongside participants as they travel through Park Forest’s section of the Old Plank Road Trail or simply attend Holden Park’s community gathering as spectators when the relay passes through their area.
According to the official website of Village of Park Forest, it promotes community health and engagement via dedicated commissions; has received accolades for sustainability efforts; aims to bolster economic conditions through collaboration; operates under a council-manager government structure; shows leadership in sustainability initiatives such as supporting national climate agreements; and provides educational opportunities like its Civic Leadership Academy.
